title: The leanest cuts of pork

seo.title: Leanest pork cuts: fat, calories and protein per 100 g
seo.meta_description: Cooked pork tenderloin has about 3.5 g fat/100 g, while trimmed loin cuts commonly provide roughly 4.5–7 g. Compare lean portions in the same cooked state.
seo.search_intent: Identify pork cuts with the least fat and compare their protein, fat and calories.

excerpt: Pork tenderloin is among the leanest pork cuts: a USDA roasted lean-only reference provides about 143 calories, 26.2 g protein and 3.5 g fat per 100 g. Trimmed center loin is around 4.7 g fat, while other lean loin references fall around 5–7 g depending on trim and cooking.
content_html:
“Pork” does not predict fat content very well. Tenderloin and well-trimmed loin can contain under 5 g fat per 100 g cooked, while other cuts retain substantially more visible and intramuscular fat.

Representative cooked lean references per 100 g

USDA cutCaloriesProteinFat
Tenderloin, lean only, roasted~143~26.2 g~3.5 g
Boneless center loin, lean only, pan-broiled~162~30.0 g~4.7 g
Boneless sirloin chop~170~28.2 g~5.5 g
Boneless top loin, lean only~173~27.6 g~6.1 g
Bone-in center loin, lean only~180~26.8 g~7.3 g

The cooking methods are not identical, but the values clearly place tenderloin and trimmed loin at the lean end.

“Lean only” matters

A chop with its outer fat eaten is not nutritionally equivalent to the same chop after trimming. USDA entries that specify separable lean only help distinguish muscle from removable fat.

Protein stays high

Tenderloin at only 3.5 g fat still provides about 26 g protein/100 g. The lean center-loin reference reaches about 30 g, roughly 4 g more protein per 100 g.

Cooking can erase the calorie advantage

Breading, frying or rich sauces change the final dish. Fifteen grams of oil can add up to about 135 calories if all of it remains in the food.

Bottom line

Pork tenderloin and well-trimmed loin are the most predictably lean choices. Look at the specific cut, visible fat and cooking method rather than judging pork as one category.

faq.question: What is the leanest pork cut?
faq.answer: Tenderloin is among the leanest; a cooked USDA lean-only reference has about 3.5 g fat per 100 g.

faq.question: Is pork loin lean?
faq.answer: Well-trimmed cooked loin references commonly provide about 4.5–7 g fat per 100 g.

faq.question: Does trimming visible fat matter?
faq.answer: Yes. The fat value can change substantially depending on whether separable fat is included.
